description: Site-specific failed approaches to avoid repeating

failed_approaches.approach: Using responsive PID allocation (pid_kp=0.001) to improve PFT#10 biomass
failed_approaches.why_failed: PID responds to light stress (dominant signal) rather than P stress when total productivity is extremely low, leading to maladaptive leaf allocation that worsens both leaf and root biomass
alternatives: Fix P starvation first before optimizing allocation strategy
Sequential targeted parameter modifications rather than allocation optimization

failed_approaches.approach: Applying SPSA optimization directly to underperforming PFTs without mechanistic diagnosis
failed_approaches.why_failed: SPSA assumes near local optimum but PFT#10 has mechanistic bottlenecks (zero P uptake, wrong turnover) that must be fixed first. Gradient-based optimization fails when applied to wrong parameter set
alternatives: Diagnostic-driven refinement workflow
Sequential bottleneck removal
Targeted parameter changes based on mechanistic understanding

failed_approaches.approach: Single-variable optimization (Method 1) focusing only on PFT#10 fineroot biomass
failed_approaches.why_failed: Achieved high PFT#10 fineroot (80% of target) by suppressing PFT#9 (93% underestimate) and causing massive AGB overshoot (13.7×)
alternatives: Multi-PFT balanced optimization (Method 2)
Hybrid parameter modification approach

failed_approaches.approach: mod5-7 parameter modification tests based on mod4 foundation with 90% MR reduction
failed_approaches.why_failed: mod4 foundation had ecosystem collapse from 90% maintenance respiration reduction, making all subsequent tests invalid
alternatives: mod8-10 tests from original 3643 baseline
Hybrid approach from Set #3930

failed_approaches.approach: Equal weighting of all 9 outputs in composite NRMSE (Method 2)
failed_approaches.why_failed: Severely underestimates PFT#10 fineroot (9% of target) while achieving good shrub performance
alternatives: Weighted NRMSE with PFT#10 emphasis
Method 1.5 with AGB constraints
Hybrid parameter modification

failed_approaches.approach: Modifying cross-PFT parameters to help target PFT
failed_approaches.why_failed: Parameters that help one PFT harm others, creating optimization conflicts
alternatives: Focus on PFT-specific parameters only
Multi-objective optimization for compromise values

failed_approaches.approach: Using shared phenology parameters for optimization
failed_approaches.why_failed: Shared parameters have opposite effects on different PFTs, cannot simultaneously optimize all
alternatives: Make phenology parameters PFT-specific
Accept sub-optimal performance for some PFTs
Find compromise values

failed_approaches.approach: Using simplified PyModel for phenology calibration
failed_approaches.why_failed: Missing cold status state machine logic - GDD accumulated continuously instead of conditionally, causing 31-day MAE vs 2.2-day MAE for full model
alternatives: Use full PyModel with complete state machine
Validate surrogate models thoroughly before calibration

failed_approaches.approach: Morris sampling with num_levels=8 for exponential phenology parameters
failed_approaches.why_failed: Grid resolution too coarse - optimal phen_c value fell between grid points, causing all 4,170 parameter combinations to miss optimal phenology
alternatives: Increase num_levels to 16 or 32 for sensitive parameters
Follow Morris screening with continuous optimization
Use adaptive/hierarchical sampling

failed_approaches.approach: Including 2000-2001 in phenology calibration
failed_approaches.why_failed: Initialization artifacts from nchilldays=0 startup caused wrong GDD threshold calculations in first two years
alternatives: Exclude initialization years from calibration
Run 1999 spin-up to accumulate proper chilling days
Use 2002-2019 as calibration period

failed_approaches.approach: Storage cushion hypothesis as primary bottleneck
failed_approaches.why_failed: Storage cushion creates targets but is irrelevant when NPP is negative - storage is being depleted, not filled. Absolute storage deficit is small (~0.3 g C/m²)
alternatives: Focus on making NPP positive first
Arctic-specific GPP parameterization

failed_approaches.approach: PID controller root over-allocation as primary bottleneck
failed_approaches.why_failed: PID controller adjusts allocation of positive NPP only. When NPP is negative, PID is not active and allocation fractions become meaningless
alternatives: Address negative NPP root cause
Increase spring GPP capacity

failed_approaches.approach: Nitrogen limitation hypothesis
failed_approaches.why_failed: N supply (0.67 g N/m²) far exceeds demand (0.002 g N/m²) due to low stoich_nitr_leaf_10 (0.00122). N ratio >1000x sufficient
alternatives: Focus on carbon availability
Photosynthesis temperature response

failed_approaches.approach: Further reduction of maintenance respiration via maintresp_nonleaf_baserate parameter
failed_approaches.why_failed: Parameter already at lower bound (1.296e-6 gC/gN/s), 49% below default, cannot be reduced further within Morris parameter space
alternatives: Temperature-dependent maintenance respiration code modification
Expand Morris parameter bounds

failed_approaches.approach: Increasing photosynthetic capacity via leaf_slatop_10 parameter
failed_approaches.why_failed: Parameter at lower bound (0.00853 m²/gC), representing thickest possible leaves with minimum photosynthetic area per unit carbon, cannot increase GPP capacity further
alternatives: Arctic-specific photosynthesis parameterization in code
Expand upper SLA bounds to allow thinner leaves

failed_approaches.approach: Further phenology optimization via parameter adjustment
failed_approaches.why_failed: Phenology already optimized on Dec 7 with RMSE 4.2 days, Case #3643 parameters very close to optimal values, phenology timing is not the constraint
alternatives: Focus on carbon balance code modifications
Accept current phenology as adequate

failed_approaches.approach: Changing Arctic reference temperature from 20°C to 10°C
failed_approaches.why_failed: At spring temperature T=5°C, changing reference to 10°C increases MR scaling from 0.35 to 0.71, doubling MR and worsening carbon balance
alternatives: Use lower reference temperature (5°C)
Implement dormancy mechanism
Combined dormancy + lower reference approach

failed_approaches.approach: Parameter optimization alone to solve spring carbon starvation
failed_approaches.why_failed: maintresp_nonleaf_baserate already at lower bound (1.296e-6, 49% below default) but still produces MR > GPP in spring
alternatives: Code modifications for dormancy scaling
Arctic-specific temperature response
Enhanced Arctic photosynthesis

failed_approaches.approach: Extreme range expansion of fates_cnp_vmax_p by 5 orders of magnitude (5e-11 to range [5e-09, 5e-03], center 1e-06) for PFT 10 in experiment s0311h01_c0_exp1
failed_approaches.why_failed: Hard model crash with no output file generated. The 5-order-of-magnitude expansion of the phosphorus uptake Vmax parameter drove numerical instability in the ECA competition solver, causing mass balance violations in CNP cycling and a complete simulation failure before any output could be written.
alternatives: Restrict fates_cnp_vmax_p exploration to [5e-12, 5e-10] (1 order of magnitude on each side of default)
Use log-scale perturbations of fates_cnp_vmax_p with maximum step size of 0.5 log-units per experiment iteration
If P uptake needs to increase substantially, consider adjusting fates_cnp_eca_km_ps (half-saturation constant) instead, which has lower sensitivity to numerical instability
Run a stability sweep with single-parameter perturbations of fates_cnp_vmax_p at 2x, 5x, 10x, 50x, 100x default to identify the crash threshold before attempting range expansion

failed_approaches.approach: Extreme multi-order-of-magnitude range expansion of fates_cnp_vmax_p (5e-09 to 5e-03 for PFT 10, 5e-07 to 5e-03 for PFT 9) combined with coordinated l2fr_ini reduction in a single experiment
failed_approaches.why_failed: The proposed parameter ranges are too far from physically plausible defaults for Arctic tundra PFTs, causing ECA solver divergence or soil P pool exhaustion that aborts the simulation before any output can be written. The combination of extreme vmax_p with l2fr_ini reduction creates contradictory nutrient uptake signals that compound numerical instability. No output file was generated, confirming catastrophic failure rather than degraded performance.
alternatives: Perform incremental vmax_p increases of 1 order of magnitude per experiment step, verifying model stability at each step before proceeding
Use sensitivity analysis (Morris screening) with narrow perturbation ranges (±50% of default) to identify the stable operating envelope before range expansion
Modify vmax_p for only one PFT at a time to isolate ECA competition effects
If l2fr_ini must be co-varied with vmax_p, compute net uptake capacity change first and ensure it remains within 1 order of magnitude of default net uptake
Start from a known-stable intermediate parameter set rather than attempting to jump directly to extreme bounds

failed_approaches.approach: Simultaneous multi-PFT fates_cnp_vmax_p range expansion (>3 orders of magnitude) coordinated with fates_l2fr reduction, using placeholder 'RANGE EXPANSION REQUIRED' values instead of concrete numbers.
failed_approaches.why_failed: The experiment was malformed at submission (placeholder values rather than concrete numbers) and the intended parameter changes were too extreme for the ECA solver to handle. No NC output was produced, confirming a model crash rather than a poor-fit result. This represents a complete experimental design failure: the experiment was neither executable nor interpretable.
alternatives: Test fates_cnp_vmax_p for each PFT individually, starting with a 10x increase from baseline and validating model execution before expanding further.
Use a binary search between the original value and the target maximum to find the stability boundary for each PFT.
First establish stable l2fr values in isolation, then introduce vmax_p changes in a subsequent experiment.
For PFT 10 (pathologically low at 5e-11), start with 5e-10 as a conservative first step and verify ECA competition outputs are physically reasonable before proceeding to 1e-09 or higher.
Run a single-PFT sensitivity scan (e.g., 5 values spanning 3 orders of magnitude for one PFT at a time) to map the stability envelope before multi-PFT combinations.

failed_approaches.approach: Coordinated multi-PFT vmax_p range expansion (4-6 orders of magnitude) combined with l2fr contraction for shared PFTs in a single experiment, with the intent of simultaneously relieving P limitation and correcting root allocation bias.
failed_approaches.why_failed: The experiment produced no NC output file, indicating a catastrophic model crash rather than a degraded run. The mechanistic cause is likely ECA solver numerical instability arising from the contradictory signals of extreme P uptake capacity (high vmax_p) paired with structurally reduced fine root biomass (low l2fr). Applying this across 3 PFTs simultaneously compounded the instability. The approach conflates two independent calibration objectives (P uptake capacity and root allocation balance) that need to be addressed sequentially, not simultaneously.
alternatives: Stage vmax_p expansion incrementally: first expand by 1-2 orders of magnitude for one PFT (e.g., PFT 10 as most deficient), verify model stability and output, then proceed to next PFT.
Decouple the l2fr and vmax_p adjustments into separate experiments: first fix l2fr for PFT 9 alone (holding vmax_p constant), evaluate root allocation metrics, then address vmax_p separately.

If both parameters must move, ensure they move in a mechanistically consistent direction: if l2fr decreases (fewer roots per leaf), reduce vmax_p proportionally to maintain consistent total P uptake flux, rather than increasing it.
Consider reducing fates_cnp_pid_kp as a stabilizing first step before any vmax_p range expansion, to give the allocation PID controller more headroom to respond to the new uptake signal.
Use a factorial design with small perturbations (±50% rather than orders of magnitude) to first establish the sensitivity surface before attempting large range expansions.

failed_approaches.approach: Simultaneous multi-order-of-magnitude expansion of fates_cnp_vmax_p across multiple PFTs (7, 9, 10) combined with fates_allom_l2fr contraction for PFT9 and fates_cnp_eca_km_p downward shift for PFT10 in a single experiment
failed_approaches.why_failed: The compound parameter modifications violated ECA solver numerical stability constraints. The model produced no NC output (catastrophic crash), indicating the failure occurred before any simulation timestep completed. The root cause is the divergence between vmax_p (increased by 3-5 orders of magnitude) and km_p (decreased), creating a near-singular uptake response in the ECA competition framework. This is compounded by the l2fr contraction creating discontinuous fine root pool states. The experiment was overspecified—too many large changes simultaneously make it impossible to diagnose which parameter caused the crash.
alternatives: Stage the experiment: first test fates_cnp_vmax_p for a single PFT (e.g., PFT10 only) at moderate increase (1e-09 to 1e-08) to confirm model stability
If increasing vmax_p, keep eca_km_p at baseline or increase proportionally to maintain a stable vmax/km ratio
Apply fates_allom_l2fr contraction for PFT9 in a separate experiment from vmax_p modifications to isolate effects
Use a factorial design with single-parameter perturbations first to identify safe operating ranges before combining parameters
Validate vmax_p range by starting at current value and increasing by 10x increments with model-stability checks at each step
For arctic mycorrhizal adaptation hypothesis (lower km_p), test it independently with PFT10 only and current vmax_p values before combining with vmax_p expansion

failed_approaches.approach: Simultaneous large-magnitude range restructuring of 6 coupled CNP and allocation parameters (vmax_p x3 PFTs, l2fr, eca_km_p, phos_store_ratio) in a single experiment with no incremental validation
failed_approaches.why_failed: The experiment produced a catastrophic crash (no NC output file) before any metrics could be evaluated. The most probable mechanism is ECA solver divergence caused by the contradictory combination of drastically reduced fineroot biomass (l2fr contraction for PFT 9) and massively expanded P uptake capacity (vmax_p expansion), compounded by runaway luxury P storage (phos_store_ratio elevation). There is zero diagnostic information to guide parameter adjustment because the simulation did not complete.
alternatives: Stage 1: Validate fates_allom_l2fr contraction for PFT 9 alone (18.31 -> 8.0) and confirm FATES_FROOTC and FATES_L2FR outputs are physically reasonable before touching vmax_p
Stage 2: After l2fr is stable, test vmax_p expansion for a single PFT (e.g., PFT 10 only) with a conservative 1 order of magnitude increase, not 4
Stage 3: Only after both l2fr and vmax_p are individually validated, test their interaction for PFT 9 with modest coordinated adjustments
Use single-PFT sensitivity experiments (Morris one-at-a-time) to establish safe operating ranges for each parameter before multi-PFT optimization
Set vmax_p upper bounds to no more than 10x baseline in initial range expansion experiments, expanding further only after confirming numerical stability

failed_approaches.approach: Direct range expansion of fates_cnp_vmax_p from 5e-11 baseline to center value 1e-06 (5 orders of magnitude increase) for PFT 10 in a single experiment step.
failed_approaches.why_failed: Model crashed catastrophically with no NC output file produced. The ECA phosphorus competition solver cannot handle vmax_p values that produce P uptake fluxes exceeding available soil pool sizes within a timestep. The 5-order-of-magnitude jump bypassed any numerical stability regime and caused a runtime error before any model output was generated.
alternatives: Incremental stepping: Test vmax_p at 5e-10, 5e-09, 5e-08, 5e-07 sequentially, checking NC output and ECA solver convergence diagnostics at each step before proceeding.
Binary search stability: Use bisection between 5e-11 (stable) and 1e-06 (crashed) to find the maximum stable vmax_p value — start at geometric midpoint ~2e-09.
Log-space sensitivity: Conduct Morris or Sobol sensitivity analysis using log-transformed vmax_p with narrow initial bounds (1 order of magnitude) before expanding to the full proposed range.
Check ECA solver timestep: Investigate whether reducing the ECA solver tolerance or adding a flux limiter in the FATES code would allow stable simulation at higher vmax_p values.

Examine soil P pool size: If target is to remove P limitation, consider modifying soil P availability parameters (e.g., initial P pools) rather than vmax_p alone, which may achieve the biological goal without triggering numerical instability.

failed_approaches.approach: Multi-order-of-magnitude range expansion of fates_cnp_vmax_p (>2 orders) for arctic PFTs 9 and 10 combined with coordinated l2fr_ini adjustment in a single experiment
failed_approaches.why_failed: Catastrophic numerical failure — no NC output file generated. The ECA/RD phosphorus uptake solver cannot handle vmax_p values spanning 5 orders of magnitude from the calibrated base. The model crashes before producing any diagnostics, making this approach uninformative for calibration and impossible to score against targets.
alternatives: Incremental single-order-of-magnitude vmax_p expansion: test PFT 10 at 5e-10 first, confirm model runs, then 5e-09
Isolate vmax_p sensitivity for each PFT separately before combining PFT 9 and PFT 10 changes
Run Morris sensitivity analysis on vmax_p within a conservative ±50% range around current values before expanding bounds
If large vmax_p is mechanistically required, first identify and adjust ECA competition parameters (e.g., Km half-saturation) to maintain numerical stability at high vmax_p
Use a bisection search: test midpoint between known-good and proposed-bad values to find the stability boundary

failed_approaches.approach: Simultaneous extreme range expansion of fates_cnp_vmax_p for PFTs 7, 9, and 10 with magnitude changes of 3-5 orders of magnitude in a single experiment
failed_approaches.why_failed: Complete model crash (no NetCDF output generated) due to numerical instability in ECA competition solver or stoichiometric cascade failure triggered by unrealistic phosphorus uptake rates. The simultaneous modification of three PFTs with extreme value changes made it impossible to isolate the failing component and prevented any useful diagnostic information from being captured.
alternatives: Incremental single-PFT vmax_p expansion: modify one PFT at a time with maximum 1 order of magnitude change per step, validating numerical stability before proceeding
For PFT 10 specifically, first verify whether 5e-11 is intentional (non-vascular plant, lichen) vs. erroneous default before any expansion
Use fates_dev_arbitrary or diagnostic runs to probe ECA solver stability at intermediate vmax_p values before committing to full range expansion
Coordinate vmax_p expansion with ECA Km parameters to maintain biologically realistic uptake kinetics (Michaelis-Menten constraint: vmax/Km ratio should remain within 10x of baseline)

failed_approaches.approach: Coordinated simultaneous multi-PFT fates_cnp_vmax_p range expansion (orders of magnitude) combined with fates_allom_l2fr contraction for interdependent PFTs in a single experiment
failed_approaches.why_failed: The combination of kinetic capacity expansion (vmax_p, up to 5 orders of magnitude) and structural root allocation contraction (l2fr from 18.31 to ~4.5) created an internally inconsistent CNP-allocation state. ECA competition among multiple PFTs with simultaneously altered vmax_p values caused numerical solver instability, resulting in complete model crash with no NC output produced. This is a structural incompatibility, not a parameter value issue that can be tuned.
alternatives: Modify fates_cnp_vmax_p for one PFT at a time, with incremental steps of no more than 1 order of magnitude per experiment
If l2fr must be reduced, first reduce it alone and confirm stable output, then adjust vmax_p in a subsequent experiment
If vmax_p must be expanded by >2 orders of magnitude for PFT 10, isolate that change in its own experiment before combining with other PFT modifications
Use Latin Hypercube or Sobol sensitivity sampling within conservative bounds (±50% of baseline) before attempting range expansions
Verify structural-kinetic consistency: ensure vmax_p * FATES_FROOTC remains within physically plausible P uptake flux range before submitting

failed_approaches.approach: Simultaneous large-magnitude expansion of fates_cnp_vmax_p (4-5 orders of magnitude) across multiple PFTs (7, 9, 10) combined with fates_allom_l2fr range contraction for PFT 9 and fates_cnp_eca_km_p range shift for PFT 10 in a single experiment
failed_approaches.why_failed: Catastrophic numerical crash — no NC output file produced. The combined effect of extreme vmax_p values, reduced km_p, and inconsistent l2fr/vmax_p ratios drove the ECA solver and/or allocation solver into numerical instability (likely NaN or negative pool values) within the first few timesteps. This is a structural model stability failure, not a biological calibration failure.
alternatives: Stage experiments: first test vmax_p range expansion for each PFT individually (one PFT per run) to identify safe upper bounds before combining
Use a maximum vmax_p expansion of 1-2 orders of magnitude per experiment, not 4-5
Decouple l2fr changes from vmax_p changes: run l2fr adjustment first, verify stability, then introduce vmax_p change
When exploring large vmax_p ranges, use a logarithmic sweep with checkpointing to identify the crash threshold before committing to full range
Modify fates_cnp_eca_km_p and fates_cnp_vmax_p for the same PFT in separate experiments to isolate their individual effects on ECA solver stability

failed_approaches.approach: Simultaneous 6-parameter CNP modification with multi-order-of-magnitude vmax_p expansion (PFT 10: 5e-11 to ~1e-6), large l2fr contraction (18.31 to ~4.5), eca_km_p downshift, and phos_store_ratio upshift in a single experiment
failed_approaches.why_failed: Model crashed with no NC output file produced. The compound modifications created numerical instability, most likely in the ECA phosphorus competition solver where the simultaneous increase in vmax_p and decrease in eca_km_p produced pathological uptake rates. The experiment was annotated internally as requiring range validation before execution, indicating it was not ready for combined testing. This represents a catastrophic failure mode where not even degraded output was produced.
alternatives: Sequential single-parameter validation: first validate fates_cnp_vmax_p for PFT 10 alone with staged increases (1e-10, 1e-9, 1e-8, 1e-7) to find the numerical stability boundary
Paired mechanistically-linked modification: test fates_cnp_vmax_p + fates_cnp_eca_km_p together for PFT 10 only, with modest changes (e.g., vmax_p x5, eca_km_p x0.5) to assess ECA solver stability
Separate allocation experiment: test fates_allom_l2fr reduction for PFT 9 alone (e.g., 18.31 to 12.0 first, then 8.0) before coupling with vmax_p changes
Fractional factorial design: run 3 separate experiments each covering 2 parameters, then combine only those combinations that individually produce valid outputs
Use fates_dev_arbitrary as a diagnostic probe to isolate which parameter combination triggers the crash before committing to full experiments

failed_approaches.approach: Submit a calibration experiment with a placeholder or non-numeric parameter value (e.g., 'DIAGNOSTIC ONLY') as a stand-in for fates_cnp_vmax_p while intending to determine the actual value post-hoc from another case.
failed_approaches.why_failed: The parameter file cannot accept a non-numeric string as a valid value for fates_cnp_vmax_p. The simulation did not produce an NC output file (targets_met: 0 of 6, metrics: {}), indicating either a pre-run configuration error or a silent job failure. Diagnostic intent must be resolved before experiment submission, not after.
alternatives: Complete the diagnostic step (extract fates_cnp_vmax_p value from Case #1386) BEFORE submitting any experiment that depends on that value.
Submit a true diagnostic run first (with old_value unchanged and logging enabled) to extract reference values, then submit the calibration experiment as a separate step.
Implement a pre-submission validation check that rejects experiments with non-numeric parameter values.

Use a parameter sensitivity sweep around the old_value (5e-11) as a temporary ensemble center while the Case #1386 extraction is pending, and retroactively refine once the reference value is confirmed.

failed_approaches.approach: Submitting diagnostic placeholder strings (e.g., 'DIAGNOSTIC ONLY — extract Case #1386 value') as parameter values for fates_cnp_vmax_p and fates_allom_l2fr in a live simulation run
failed_approaches.why_failed: Non-numeric placeholder strings cannot be parsed by ELM-FATES parameter ingestion routines. The model fails before generating any output NC file, resulting in zero metrics evaluated and a completely uninformative experiment. This approach conflates the diagnostic intent (identifying a reference value) with an actual calibration run.
alternatives: Before submitting any experiment, extract the actual numeric value from Case #1386 NC/parameter files and hard-code it into the parameter modification block.
Create a dedicated pre-flight validation step that checks all parameter values are numeric (not placeholder strings) before job submission.
If the intent is purely diagnostic (reading a value from a reference case), perform the extraction as an offline analysis step — do not submit it as a simulation experiment.
Maintain a lookup table of verified parameter values from reference cases (e.g., Case #1386) so that extraction is done once and reused reliably in subsequent experiments.

failed_approaches.approach: Specifying parameter modification values as string placeholders (e.g., 'DIAGNOSTIC ONLY — extract Case #1386 value') instead of concrete numerical values when submitting experiments for execution
failed_approaches.why_failed: The simulation framework requires all parameter modifications to be valid numerical values that can be written into the FATES parameter NetCDF file. String placeholders cause the parameter file construction step to fail silently or crash, resulting in no output NC file being generated. The error 'Extracted NC file not found' is the downstream symptom of this upstream workflow misconfiguration. Zero of 6 targets were evaluated because the simulation never ran.
alternatives: Before submitting an experiment, extract the concrete numerical parameter values from Case #1386 output or parameter files and substitute them as explicit floats in the modification specification (e.g., fates_cnp_vmax_p PFT10 = 7.3e-11, fates_allom_l2fr PFT10 = 11.2, fates_allom_l2fr PFT9 = 15.6)
Implement a pre-submission validation step that checks all parameter modification values are numeric (not strings) before the experiment is dispatched to the model runner

If the intent is truly diagnostic and values are unknown, first run a separate data-extraction query against the Case #1386 ensemble database to retrieve the parameter values, record them explicitly, then formulate the experiment with those concrete values
Use a two-phase workflow: Phase 1 extracts and logs Case #1386 parameter values into the calibration memory system; Phase 2 submits the experiment with those logged values as the new ensemble center

failed_approaches.approach: Submitting experiments with placeholder/string values (e.g., 'DIAGNOSTIC ONLY — extract Case #1386 value') instead of concrete numerical parameter values for fates_cnp_vmax_p and fates_allom_l2fr, intending to resolve them post-submission.
failed_approaches.why_failed: The parameter file builder requires numerical values; string placeholders prevent valid NetCDF parameter file generation. The simulation either crashes silently or produces no output NC file, causing the extraction pipeline to report a file-not-found error. Zero targets are met because no simulation data exists. This is a pre-submission workflow error: diagnostic extraction of reference case values (e.g., Case #1386) must be completed BEFORE the experiment JSON is finalized and submitted.
alternatives: Complete the diagnostic extraction of Case #1386 parameter values (fates_cnp_vmax_p for PFT 9 and 10, fates_allom_l2fr for PFT 9 and 10) FIRST, then populate new_value fields with explicit floats before submitting.
If the intent is to inspect Case #1386 values without running a new simulation, query the existing Case #1386 NC output directly rather than creating a new experiment entry.
Implement a pre-submission validation step that rejects any experiment modification where new_value is not a finite number, catching this class of error before job submission.
Use the base case (322) run as the diagnostic reference and extract parameter values programmatically from its parameter NetCDF file rather than relying on manual lookup.

failed_approaches.approach: Submitting a multi-parameter modification experiment (fates_cnp_vmax_p PFT9/10, fates_allom_l2fr PFT9/10, fates_cnp_eca_vmax_ptase PFT10) with placeholder string values instead of resolved numeric parameter values, intending to extract target values from Case #1386 at runtime.
failed_approaches.why_failed: ELM-FATES requires all parameter values to be valid floating-point numbers at simulation launch. String placeholders cause pre-simulation failure with no NC output. The experiment confused a diagnostic intent (find best values) with an executable simulation (use those values). Zero targets were met because no simulation was ever completed.
alternatives: Step 1: Extract numeric parameter values for fates_cnp_vmax_p (PFT9, PFT10), fates_allom_l2fr (PFT9, PFT10), and fates_cnp_eca_vmax_ptase (PFT10) directly from the Case #1386 parameter file before constructing the experiment record.
Step 2: Submit a new experiment with all five parameters set to the numerically resolved Case #1386 values as the new ensemble center.
Add a pre-submission validation script that checks all new_value fields for numeric type and rejects experiments containing non-numeric entries.

If the intent is ensemble re-centering, use a dedicated re-centering workflow that programmatically reads the best-performing ensemble member's parameter file and populates a new experiment template automatically.

failed_approaches.approach: Submitting multi-parameter experiments with 'DIAGNOSTIC ONLY — extract Case #X value' placeholder strings as new_value entries, expecting the pipeline to resolve them automatically or use them as valid parameter inputs.
failed_approaches.why_failed: The calibration pipeline has no mechanism to resolve string placeholders into numeric parameter values at runtime. The parameter file was either malformed or unchanged from the base case, and no valid NC output file was generated. Zero targets were met because the simulation produced no output to evaluate. This is a pure workflow/data-management failure, not a scientific or physical modeling failure.
alternatives: Explicitly extract and record all parameter values from Case #1386 into the knowledge base before designing any dependent experiments.
Re-run experiment s0311h01_c1_exp6 with all six parameter slots filled with concrete float values sourced from Case #1386.
Implement a pre-submission validator that rejects any experiment specification containing non-numeric new_value fields.

If Case #1386 values cannot be recovered, design a targeted sensitivity run around the base-case values for these six parameters (fates_cnp_vmax_p PFTs 9/10, fates_allom_l2fr PFTs 9/10, fates_cnp_eca_vmax_ptase PFT 10, fates_cnp_eca_decompmicc PFT 7) using a ±30% Latin hypercube to identify a new ensemble center independently.
